title: AI Estate

panels.title: GPU Power

panels.title: Energy Today
panels.description: Energy since local midnight (panel pinned to now/d via timeFrom), computed with MetricsQL integrate() over the actual power samples, divided into kWh. Deliberately NOT avg_over_time(...) * $__range_s: that form extrapolates the sampled average across any unsampled hours, and on a partial-coverage day (exporter or box down for part of the day) it over-reported by ~3.4x, drifting DOWNWARD as idle samples accumulated -- caught live 2026-08-29 against a raw /api/v1/export trapezoid ground truth (integrate() matched within 0.25%). Issued as a range query reduced to its last value, per this project's standing rule for stat panels.

panels.title: VRAM / Temp
panels.description: GPU memory used (left axis, binary bytes) vs die temperature (right axis, deg C).

panels.title: Prompt vs Generation (by model)
panels.description: Five-minute prompt and generation rates by model or active lane. The log10 axis keeps low generation rates visible beside prefill-heavy prompt traffic; zero-rate idle periods are not drawn on a logarithmic axis.

panels.description: End-to-end request latency, sglang: histogram (verified live name/labels; llama.cpp lane not yet resident).

panels.title: Daily Tokens by Provider (30d)
panels.description: Stacked daily token deltas per cloud-side provider (hermes excluded -- its client-side view mixes local + cloud-routed traffic and lives in its own attribution panel below, per the spec's anti-double-count rule). Query is a direct two-point counter subtraction -- max_over_time(...) minus its 1d-offset twin, each falling back to a zero-valued series that carries the SAME labels (X or (X*0), not X or vector(0), which has no labels and silently drops any series with no exact match) -- NOT increase(). increase() was verified live against this day-granular pushed data to be unreliable (window-size-dependent, off by up to ~27x); see README troubleshooting. Filtered by the Provider / Model / Token kind dropdowns (All = the previous unfiltered behaviour).

panels.title: Cost per Day (30d)
panels.description: Daily client-side cost delta per cloud provider. Hermes is excluded to avoid double-counting its mixed local and cloud-routed client view. Uses the same two-point subtraction as the token panels, not increase(). Filtered by the Provider / Model dropdowns (cost series carry no kind label, so Token kind does not apply).

panels.title: Daily Tokens by Model (30d)
panels.description: Stacked daily token deltas per (provider, model) across cloud-side providers (hermes excluded, same anti-double-count rule as the provider panel). Same two-point max_over_time subtraction as every other counter panel here -- never increase(). Filtered by the Provider / Model / Token kind dropdowns (All = the previous unfiltered behaviour). Limited to the 12 largest series via MetricsQL topk_max(), which picks ONE series set for the whole range -- Prometheus topk() re-ranks at every step, which makes stacked daily bars flicker and mis-stack. Pick a single model in the dropdown to isolate it (e.g. gpt-6-astra).

panels.title: Cost per Day by Model (30d)
panels.description: Stacked daily USD cost deltas per (provider, model) across cloud-side providers (hermes excluded). Cost is whatever each source reports (tokscale's list-price estimate for the coding agents, OpenRouter's billed usage for the openrouter lane). Filtered by the Provider / Model dropdowns (cost series carry no kind label, so Token kind does not apply). Limited to the 12 largest series via MetricsQL topk_max(), which picks ONE series set for the whole range -- Prometheus topk() re-ranks at every step, which makes stacked daily bars flicker and mis-stack. Pick a single model in the dropdown to isolate it (e.g. gpt-6-astra).

panels.title: Month-to-Date
panels.description: Cumulative tokens since the start of the current calendar month, per cloud-side provider (hermes excluded). Panel time range is pinned to now/M via timeFrom, independent of the dashboard's own 24h default. Deliberately issued as a range query reduced to its last point, not an instant query: verified live that VictoriaMetrics' instant-query path (/api/v1/query) can return a materially wrong result for this same max_over_time+large-offset expression at the exact same evaluation instant an identical range query (/api/v1/query_range) gets exactly right against a raw-export ground truth -- a second, separate reliability finding beyond increase(); see README troubleshooting. Filtered by the Provider / Model / Token kind dropdowns (All = the previous unfiltered behaviour). Month boundary is exact: the offset side is evaluated with the @ modifier at ${__from:date:seconds} (the panel's now/M range start = local month start), not `offset $__range` -- on a step grid the offset form landed the boundary inside the previous month's last day (verified live: it counted Aug 31) and the day-aligned grid excluded today. Hourly steps keep the last point, and the sparkline, current.

panels.title: Model Breakdown (30d)
panels.description: Every (provider, model) pair with usage in the last 30 days across cloud-side providers (hermes excluded -- controller ruling: a ranked table invites cross-provider summing by eye, which recreates the double-count the anti-double-count rule prevents; hermes's per-model breakdown lives in its own panel below). Three range queries (tokens of the selected kinds, output tokens, cost), each the same two-point max_over_time subtraction as the other counter panels, issued in table format and merged: merge -> sort by time -> group by provider+model taking each value's last point -> rename -> drop zero rows -> sort by tokens -> top 20. Range queries reduced to their last point rather than instant queries, for the reason given on the Month-to-Date tile. Column headers are filterable (type a model name). Filtered by the Provider / Model / Token kind dropdowns (All = the previous unfiltered behaviour). Evaluated on a 1-minute grid over a hidden 1-hour panel range so the last point (the value shown) is within a minute of now -- on the dashboard's day-aligned grid the table stopped at the last local midnight and today's usage never appeared until tomorrow. The 30-day window comes from the query's own offset, not the panel range.

panels.title: Cost Month-to-Date
panels.description: Cumulative USD cost since the start of the current calendar month, per cloud-side provider (hermes excluded). Same now/M time override and range-query-reduced-to-last-point pattern as the token Month-to-Date tile. Filtered by the Provider / Model dropdowns (cost series carry no kind label, so Token kind does not apply). Month boundary is exact: the offset side is evaluated with the @ modifier at ${__from:date:seconds} (the panel's now/M range start = local month start), not `offset $__range` -- on a step grid the offset form landed the boundary inside the previous month's last day (verified live: it counted Aug 31) and the day-aligned grid excluded today. Hourly steps keep the last point, and the sparkline, current.

panels.title: Local vs Cloud Output (24h)
panels.description: Comparable output-token totals for the last 24 hours: server-side local generation versus client-side cloud output, plus local output share. Hermes is excluded from cloud totals to prevent double-counting its mixed routing view. Uses two-point counter subtraction rather than increase().

panels.title: Hermes Client View (30d)
panels.description: Client-side view. Daily token deltas by Hermes model/profile, as reported by tokscale's client-side view of Hermes activity (mixes local-served and cloud-routed-through-Hermes traffic). Deliberately never summed into any cross-provider total on this dashboard -- see the anti-double-count rule. Same robust subtraction pattern as the other day-granular panels, not increase(). Rendered as stacked daily bars: the data is sparse day-granular deltas, which as overlapping lines read as a tangle of spikes over empty space.

panels.title: Collector Lanes
panels.description: Latest status per known collector lane. UP means a successful sample in the last 20 minutes. NOT UP means the latest cycle failed, the lane is unconfigured, or no recent sample exists; a 30-day fallback keeps stale lane labels visible.

panels.title: Collector Freshness
panels.description: Elapsed time since each lane last succeeded. Green is under 15 minutes, yellow is 15-60 minutes, and red is over one hour. A 30-day lookback keeps stopped collectors visible; known lanes that have never succeeded are shown explicitly as NEVER.
